subject: Re: GlobalMed - Private VPC/discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@globalmed.com>, Sophia Lee <sophia.lee@globalmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: GlobalMed discovery - Private VPC recap & next steps

Hi Raj / Sophia,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to capture clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary driver: regulatory/data residency + strict PHI handling for clinical notes and patient metadata.
- Networking constraints: GlobalMed requires VPC peering or PrivateLink; no public internet egress from the processing cluster; strict IP allowlist; inbound only from static NATed IPs.
- Air-gap option: for specific sites, they may require an air-gapped deployment with offline model package delivery.
- Key security asks: SOC 2 evidence, customer-managed KMS/HSM integration, audit logs (immutable), and support for customer certs for mTLS.
- Scale expectations: initial pilot ~50 concurrent inference requests (mostly short clinical summaries), ramp to ~2k QPS over 12 months on dedicated private infra.

Open questions we flagged:
1) Which GlobalMed VPCs/regions need peering vs full private install? (Raj to confirm list)
2) Any procurement gating timelines or third-party security review windows?
3) Do you have a preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, etc.) or on-prem HSM?

Next steps:
- Redwood: share network requirements & preliminary SOW draft (attached). Action: Camila - send network checklist and draft SOW. (Attached: globalmed-network-requirements.pdf, draft-sow-globalmed.docx)
- GlobalMed: confirm VPC CIDR blocks and how many subnets/regions we must support. Action: Raj - share VPC inventory by Tue 6/29.
- Security: Redwood to prepare SOC 2 artifact list and integration notes for customer KMS; Marissa to coordinate security questionnaire.
- Follow-up call: schedule a tech deep-dive w/ GlobalMed infra and our Private Deploy team. Suggested window: week of 7/6.

Thanks - I'll follow up with the network checklist and SOW draft in a separate email.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Camila - this looks great and captures the call. A few clarifications:
- We'll need the PrivateLink option for our production region (us-west-2) and VPC peering for the pilot environment in us-east-1.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS for cloud regions; we do have HSMs in two on-prem DCs that may be needed for air-gapped sites.
- Procurement: expect an initial security review with our InfoSec team the week of 7/13; procurement timing ~4-6 weeks after InfoSec sign-off.

I'll collate the VPC CIDRs and send them by Monday. Also please include a short checklist of firewall rules / proxy egress requirements - that'll help our network team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Great - thanks Raj. Attached is the network checklist you can hand to your network team (globalmed-network-requirements.pdf) and a short private-deploy overview (redwood-private-deploy-overview.pdf).

Quick notes for your infra team:
- Egress: Redwood's Private control plane requires outbound HTTPS to a minimal set of endpoints for telemetry and control; we can support a proxy model where the control plane connection is initiated from inside your VPC (no inbound). If you need full air-gap we provide a separate on-prem bundle with offline activation.
- Ports: outbound 443 to 3 endpoints (listed in the attached checklist).
- MTLS: we support customer-provided certs at the LB and mTLS between services; our team will provide CSR templates if you need them.

I've attached the items and a short draft SOW for your review (draft-sow-globalmed.docx). If helpful, we can include optional line items for on-prem HSM integration and air-gapped model packaging.

I'll schedule the tech deep-dive for 7/7 at 10am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Cheers,
Camila
